title: Masseur schedule calendar view (month/week/day, mobile-first)
tech: React + TypeScript frontend addition, plus a small additive backend field on an existing endpoint
keyConstraints: Additive only: a NEW view inside AdminDashboard.tsx (e.g. a List/Calendar toggle), not a replacement of the existing pending-queue list -- Confirm/Decline/Cancel and their tests must be completely untouched. Show both pending and confirmed bookings on the calendar, visually distinct from each other (e.g. color/style difference so the masseur can tell a tentative request from a locked-in appointment at a glance); cancelled bookings never appear on the calendar. Required backend addition, confirmed by reading bookingService.ts: AdminBookingListItem/listBookingsForAdmin (backing GET /admin/bookings) currently returns only human-formatted strings -- startAtLocal/endAtLocal, e.g. 'Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 9:00 AM UTC' -- never a raw, parseable timestamp. A calendar needs real Date-positionable values to place events on a month/week/day grid; parsing a prose-formatted string back into a Date is fragile and exactly the kind of thing this codebase has deliberately avoided elsewhere (BookingWidget/ManageBooking always work from raw ISO strings returned by the backend and format client-side, never the reverse). Add start_at/end_at (raw UTC ISO, via row.start_at.toISOString()/row.end_at.toISOString() -- the query already selects these columns, so this is a response-mapping change only, no new SQL) alongside the existing startAtLocal/endAtLocal fields -- do not remove those, the existing list view depends on them. No backend query-param change needed: call GET /admin/bookings with no status filter (already returns everything) and filter out 'cancelled' client-side for the calendar -- avoids touching adminBookingsQuerySchema. Mobile-first is a real requirement, not a suggestion -- this is for a masseur checking their schedule primarily on a phone; design and verify the layout starting from a narrow viewport rather than adapting a desktop grid afterward.
description: Add a schedule/calendar view to the masseur admin dashboard, alongside the existing action-focused list (task 012). Scope: (1) a way to switch between the current list view and a new calendar view within AdminDashboard.tsx; (2) the calendar supports month, week, and day views, switchable by the masseur; (3) pending and confirmed bookings both render on the calendar, visually distinguished from each other, cancelled bookings excluded entirely; (4) events are positioned using the new raw start_at/end_at timestamps, never by parsing the formatted local strings; (5) mobile-first layout, since this is primarily a phone-use tool for a masseur checking their day between appointments. Out of scope for this task: the calendar is view-only in v1 -- tapping/clicking a booking can show its details (service, customer, time, status) but does not need to duplicate Confirm/Decline/Cancel inline; those actions stay in the existing list view. This keeps the action logic in exactly one place rather than two.
acceptanceCriteria: AdminDashboard gains a List/Calendar toggle (or equivalent) without altering the existing list view's behavior, markup, or passing tests
Calendar offers month, week, and day views, switchable by the masseur
Pending and confirmed bookings both appear on the calendar, visually distinguishable from each other (e.g. color or style difference); cancelled bookings are never shown
Calendar event positioning uses the new raw start_at/end_at fields -- never derived by parsing startAtLocal/endAtLocal
Layout is verified usable at a narrow (phone-width) viewport -- not solely designed desktop-first and adapted afterward

GET /admin/bookings's response includes start_at and end_at (raw UTC ISO) alongside the existing start_at_local/end_at_local; existing integration test(s) for this route still pass, plus a new assertion that the raw fields are present and correctly match the local-formatted ones
No change to the existing Confirm/Decline/Cancel flows, their UI, or their tests -- the calendar is purely additive
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in both backend/ and frontend/
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/api/client.ts and frontend/src/api/types.ts (extend AdminBooking with start_at/end_at)
frontend/package.json (only if a calendar library is added -- see open question below)
securityConsiderations: None beyond what already governs GET /admin/bookings (requireMasseurAuth + adminRateLimit, unchanged). Purely additive and read-only -- no new mutation surface, and no new data exposure: the raw timestamps were already fully derivable from the existing local-formatted strings, just inconveniently.
openQuestion: Build the month/week/day calendar grid from scratch, or bring in a small, well-established calendar library (e.g. react-big-calendar)? This project has a consistent 'minimal new dependencies' precedent (tasks 010/012/013 all avoided a routing library, for instance), but it also has a real history of subtle date/timezone bugs from hand-rolled logic -- the DST-boundary test case in task 004, and the UTC-vs-provider-timezone display incident found during manual testing. Month/week/day grid math (leap years, week-start conventions, day-in-month positioning, DST transitions across a displayed week) is meaningfully more complex than anything hand-rolled elsewhere in this codebase so far. Architect should weigh reinventing that (real correctness risk, more code to maintain) against a maintained library (bundle size, an actual new dependency, less control over exact mobile styling) and give an explicit recommendation with reasoning -- not default silently to either side.
